hero.headline: If You Got an Offer Tomorrow, Would You Know What You'd *Actually Keep*?
hero.subhead: For US business owners 52–67 running a $3M–$10M company and thinking about selling or transitioning in the next 12–36 months: get a defendable valuation range, a clear after-tax net-proceeds picture, and one coordinated plan — instead of siloed advisors and vague “you'll be fine” answers.

problem.title: Most Owners Don't Have a Retirement Problem. They Have a *Coordination* Problem.

items.title: No One Is Quarterbacking
items.body: You have a CPA, attorney, banker, financial advisor, and insurance agent — but they each work their own lane and nobody owns the combined outcome.

items.title: Your Number Is Fuzzy
items.body: You don't know what the business is really worth, what buyers will scrutinize, or what you'll net after taxes, fees, and deal terms.

items.title: Succession & Family Fairness
items.body: If one child is in the business and others aren't, “equal” and “fair” aren't the same — and the wrong structure can strain cash flow or fracture the family.

problem.transition: The best exits are *built years in advance* — with a plan that raises value and reduces risk before a buyer ever shows up.

audience.title: Who This Is *Built For*

items.title: Founders & CEOs (52–67)
items.body: Owners of a stable, well-known company in a second-act planning window — sell in 12–36 months or transition to a successor.

items.title: $3M–$10M in Revenue
items.body: Roughly $600K–$2.5M EBITDA, with most of your net worth still tied up in the business.

items.title: Family on the Line
items.body: A potential successor child plus others who aren't in the business — creating fairness, estate, and cash-flow pressure.

items.title: Ready for a Real Plan
items.body: Decisive once you trust the process; you want numbers you can defend and a coordinated team — not guesswork.

audience.notFor: This isn't for early-stage owners with no real enterprise value yet, or owners who already have one cohesive, tax-smart exit plan with a quarterback in place.

faqs.q: I already have advisors — why do I need this?
faqs.a: Most owners do. The issue isn't whether you have people; it's whether anyone is responsible for the combined outcome, with dates and accountability. This aligns your existing team around one plan.

faqs.q: I'm too busy to start a big project.
faqs.a: That's exactly why we work in 90-day sprints — small, high-impact moves that reduce chaos instead of adding to it.

faqs.q: Is this a pitch for a financial product?
faqs.a: No. We start with a clarity call and assessments to find the gaps and map a plan. Any strategy is built around your business, taxes, and family — never a cookie-cutter product.

faqs.q: What if my child takes over and the others feel shorted?
faqs.a: Naming that early is how you prevent a permanent family fracture. We map fairness on paper — estate equalization, governance, and cash-flow protection — before it becomes personal.

faqs.q: I'm not ready to sell yet — is it too early?
faqs.a: 12–36 months out is the ideal window. The earlier you start, the more options you keep around taxes, successor planning, and value drivers.

faqs.q: What does the clarity call cost?
faqs.a: The initial Tax-Smart Exit Clarity Call is complimentary, with no obligation.
